demand_periods.basis: First 12 service months after connection: monthly average of the adoption curve, with daily/weekly average equivalents (365 days/year). Calendar labels locate standard 365/12-day energy months; not dated billing forecasts. No seasonality is modeled.

evaluation.interval_method: 10th/90th quantile regressors with nonnegative normalized split-conformal expansion; point included in bounds before calibration and evaluation.
limitations: No real metered sites were used.
Test sites come from the same synthetic generator; field accuracy is unknown.
Growth and finance are conditional scenarios, not validated forecasts.
Nominal coverage applies under distributional assumptions, not arbitrary new communities.

selection.source: 60-site internal holdout inside the 300 training sites

stress_test.description: Synthetic held-out outcomes increased by 25%; inputs unchanged. Illustrates sensitivity to generator shift.

Resource assessment, network design and hourly generation/storage dispatch

findings.action: Compare staged construction and productive-use commitments. Spare capacity can support future growth.
findings.detail: The low case leaves part of the entered annual energy capacity unused.
findings.title: Potential over-sizing

methods.finance: Three-year NPV uses end-of-month operating surplus discounted with the annual effective rate, less entered initial project capex. It is before financing and tax, with no terminal value, replacements, expansion capex or residual asset value. It is a limited 36-month screen, not a whole-life project or equity NPV. Debt coverage and cash after debt use the stated monthly debt payment; no loan amortization is inferred. Prices, costs and capacity stay fixed. Missing budgets produce no cost/NPV/payback claim. Zero extra productive-use costs are assumptions, not verified estimates.
methods.growth: Post-connection scenario: the model's current-input estimate is used as an assumed mature-demand reference, not a measured mature load. Household connections, household appliance use and existing non-household use follow separate smooth S-shaped ramps from Month 1 to the chosen maturity month. Community counts and target uptake/appliance index describe the mature reference. Annual household/business growth compounds from Month 1 in addition to adoption; use it for underlying expansion, not the same adoption twice. New productive equipment starts once at the beginning of its selected service year, at full assumed unit use, then follows business growth. Year 1 totals are calculated from the ramp, not forced back to the old forecast. Months are 365/12-day energy equivalents; calendar labels anchor service months, not actual billing-day totals. Reference bounds are propagated under identical assumptions and do not cover uncertain adoption, growth or inputs. This curve is not validated against metered post-connection sites.
methods.productive: Each option is a static one-unit comparison against average Year 1 demand, not a staged adoption forecast. It independently adds one unit at baseline monthly energy. Ranked by added developer operating contribution after variable and entered extra operating costs. Support costs belong to the developer, not the productive business. Simple payback assumes constant contribution and excludes discounting, tax, financing, replacements and supply upgrades; values with a supply gap are provisional. Options are not additive or adoption recommendations.
methods.scenarios: Low/Expected/High multiply all expected monthly demand, including future productive-use additions. These are editable what-if cases, not probabilities or the calibrated prediction interval.
methods.sizing: Energy utilization uses served energy / entered annual customer-side energy capacity. Firm power is compared with illustrative monthly typical-day peaks, not annual maximum demand. Unused capacity is potential over-sizing, not proven waste. Capacity-linked capital × unused energy share is an allocation proxy, not recoverable savings. Energy and power gaps can coexist with spare capacity. No dispatch or equipment sizing is performed.

finance.basis: Year 1 average of monthly cash calculations; supply limits applied month by month. Peak fields use the highest monthly typical-day peak.

forecast.range_basis: Propagated reference range; not calibrated for post-connection growth

lender_explanation: Shops account for about 33% of the transparent Year 1 baseline. More customers or more equipment can increase demand, but these counts still need verification.

Demand starts at about 3,773 kWh in service Month 1 and reaches about 13,661 kWh in Month 36 under this scenario. Household connections begin at 35% of the target and appliance use at 60%; both reach their target in Month 24.

Household expansion is assumed at 8% per year and non-household expansion at 12%. These are editable assumptions, not measured trends. Lower use or slower adoption can reduce cash available for debt; faster use can exceed supply.

Public building/service records suggest inputs, not consumption. The model was trained on synthetic data. Check actual customers, utility coverage, productive-user commitments and financing terms before relying on the result. These baseline explanations are not proven causes or exact ML feature attribution.

provenance.notice: Fictional community. Synthetic evidence only; model not validated against real metered sites. Local public detections may initialize inputs; national indicators do not change the forecast. Neither validates consumption. Financial inputs are unverified.

sharing_proposal.future_curve_study: For a future authorized curve study, prepare restricted site-month aggregates for the first 36 service months, connection month, active customers by group, outages and consistent baseline inputs. These monthly files are not accepted by the current annual CSV uploader.
sharing_proposal.minimum_data: Current supported template: anonymous site ID, country, 12 complete historical months' start/end, total customer-side kWh, and the nine matching community inputs. The operator must verify definition/period consistency and avoid identifiable small groups. Do not add extra columns; the importer rejects them.

references.title: NIST SP 800-188: de-identification and disclosure-risk governance

sharing_proposal.status: Proposal only — no operator integration or hosted secure portal exists

steps.detail: Operator and project owner approve the evaluation purpose, permitted fields, recipients, retention period and deletion process before sharing. Confirm applicable requirements with the responsible data-protection/legal owner; this proposal is not compliance certification.
steps.title: Agree the purpose and authority

steps.detail: Keep raw customer readings with the operator. Export site-level totals only. Exclude names, phone numbers, meter/account IDs, household coordinates, payment records and interval-level household traces. Review small sites and rare business combinations for disclosure risk; merge or withhold unsafe groups.
steps.title: Aggregate at the operator

steps.detail: Assign random study site IDs. Keep the mapping to real locations with the operator, separate from the evaluation extract. Replacing names with codes does not guarantee anonymity. Limit country, timing and customer-group details to what the approved study needs.
steps.title: Use protected site identifiers

steps.detail: Before training or tuning, split by entire site, ideally also operator. Never put months from one site into both training and test sets. Record the split manifest, model/data versions, coverage, outages, connection dates and input timing. Do not tune on the final held-out results.
steps.title: Freeze independent holdouts

steps.detail: Proposed hosted workflow: authenticated, encrypted transfer to a restricted research workspace, named access, audit logs and a fixed deletion deadline. Those controls are not implemented here. This MVP processes the approved CSV locally in memory, does not persist the upload and does not send it to public providers. Do not expose this local server publicly or upload identifiable data.
steps.title: Transfer only approved aggregates

steps.detail: Return MAE, weighted error, bias and range coverage with site counts and limitations. Review aggregate results before release. Delete working extracts on the agreed schedule and document completion. Current CSV comparison is an annual-average frozen-model diagnostic; validating the new ramp requires separate monthly post-connection records and a held-out study.
steps.title: Publish metrics, not customer data
